lines: A live race now starts together: a countdown in the lobby, and every rider's clock on the same server time.
At three seconds the countdown covers the lobby, ready or not: three, two, one, and Go.
At Go the race opens, joins its session again on its own connection, and hears the start as the server's time.
Its clock runs from that start, corrected by the measured offset, so a rider who opens late reads the same time.
The countdown fills every screen, from a phone to a desktop.
What the tests prove: three, two, one and Go, the seat kept past the start, and every clock on server time.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
